items.title: Theorem 16.6.6 (2017: 16.8), the invariant $\Phi_{(f,o)}$ of a polyfold Fredholm section

book.label: §16.6, Theorem 16.6.6, p. 739 (2017: Theorem 16.8)
book.statement: $\partial Z=\emptyset$, $f$ oriented, compact solution set, $(n,U)$ controls compactness, $\lambda$ controlled by $(n,U)$, $(f,\lambda)$ in general position: the branched integrals over $\lambda\circ f$ define a map on cohomology, independent of $\lambda$.

lean.statement:
Part III wave 6 (`Chapter16/P3W6S6_Theorem16_6_6.lean`), on the polyfold: the integrals $\int$, $\oint$ of `CompactOrientedSuborbifold c m` are additive and well defined (`integral_mk_rep`: in every model the polyfold integral is the ep-level integral of Definition 9.5.6); for `c.boundary = ∅` and partitions of unity, $\int d\eta = \oint d\eta = 0$ (`OrientedSuborbifold.integral_d_eq_zero`, `integralEff_d_eq_zero`, from Theorem 16.4.6), hence **`integral_add_d`**, `integralEff_add_d`: the integrals depend only on $[\tau]$. `HasCobordism`, `HasCobordismEff` and **`integral_eq_of_hasCobordism`**, **`integralEff_eq_of_hasCobordismEff`** (Theorem 9.5.18 on $Y$): cobordant perturbations give equal integrals of closed forms; `hasCobordism_refl`, `hasCobordismEff_refl`. Bundle level: `OrientedPerturbation s m` (a compact oriented suborbifold with $\theta = \lambda \circ f$), `IsAdmissible n U`; **`theorem_16_6_6_statement s n U m IsInherited`** ((i) $\int(\tau + d\eta) = \int\tau$ and $\oint(\tau + d\eta) = \oint\tau$; (ii) for two admissible perturbations with the inherited orientation, equal $\int$ and $\oint$ of closed $\tau$) and **`theorem_16_6_6_hyp`** from `hPU` and `hcob`, `hcobEff` (cobordisms between any two admissible inherited-orientation perturbations); `theorem_16_6_6_hyp_hcob_witness`.

The earlier reduction: `ScPlusMultisection.IsControlledBy` ($n(\lambda)\le1$, dom-supp $\subseteq U$); `theorem_16_6_6_reduction` (in every structure $S\in\bar c$ the representatives satisfy $\partial X=\emptyset$, Fredholm, `HasCompactSolutionSetEp`, `ControlsCompactness` for `(normOf n, γπ⁻¹U)`, $N(\Lambda)\le1$, dom-supp$(\Lambda)\subseteq\gamma\pi^{-1}U$: the hypotheses of §§15.3–15.4); `exists_generalPosition_hyp` (from `theorem_15_3_7_statement` in a model: a structurable $\lambda$ controlled by $(n,U)$ with $n(\lambda)<1$, representative transversal and in general position).

diff: Proved without the cobordism: well-definedness of the integrals (independent of representative and model) and dependence only on $[\tau]$. Independence of $\lambda$ rests on `hcob`/`hcobEff` (the cobordism of Corollary 15.4.4, gap G.182) and on `IsInherited`, a parameter for the orientation inherited from $(f, o)$ (Theorem 15.4.1 at the polyfold level with the transport of orientations; gaps G.159, G.175, G.176). The theorem holds for every predicate `IsInherited`.

Added: `hPU`, partitions of unity on $Z$ (the hypothesis of Stokes, Theorem 16.4.6; witness `theorem_16_4_6_hyp_witness`). The cobordism hypotheses have only the self-cobordism witness (`theorem_16_6_6_hyp_hcob_witness`, $\tilde\Theta = 0$), and no concrete strong polyfold bundle with an admissible oriented perturbation of nonempty support is built: the statement is nonvacuous only through these witnesses (weak). The text's $f$ oriented, compact solution set and $(n, U)$ enter only through the perturbations and the cobordism.

Readings: the degree $k$ is the dimension $m+1 \ge 1$ of $\hat\theta$ (the case $k = 0$ needs the 0-dimensional branched integral, gap G.188); "$(f, \lambda)$ in general position" is read in one model (invariance under generalized isomorphisms is gap G.187); "independent of $\lambda$" is equality over any two admissible perturbations with the inherited orientation. The model-level target is `corollary_15_4_4_statement` (V15.37).
